summary: path-stream-utils-testmetest ships opaque 33MB payload auto-executed at install via native addon dropper
details: package.json's postinstall hook invokes init() on a shipped native addon (addon.node for Linux, addon_win.node for Windows). The Linux addon imports fork/setsid/execlp/chmod and contains format strings '%s/.napi_cache' and '/tmp/.%u' — a dropper pattern that reads the 33MB opaque.napi_cache bundled in the tarball, stages it to /tmp/.<pid>, chmods it executable, and launches it as a detached (fork+setsid) process at npm install time. The addon also probes a wide set of CI, container, sandbox, and debugger indicators (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, TRAVIS, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, NETLIFY, VERCEL, SANDBOX; /proc/1/cgroup, /proc/1/cmdline, /proc/self/status TracerPid, /proc/self/maps; docker/containerd/kubepod keywords) to suppress execution inside analysis environments while still firing on developer workstations. The package.json flag "stub": true and the README describing this as a 'Temporary Holding Version' / 'placeholder for staged publishing' contradict the tarball contents (712KB Windows PE, a Linux ELF, and a 33MB opaque.napi_cache blob auto-executed on install), a cover-story framing consistent with staged-publish supply-chain attacks.
